standard_prerequisites.use: Lines 2191-2193: the map f is defined as sending each k to the tuple at the k-th position of exactly this sequence - the whole proof lives on the displayed exhibit.

core_obligations: Definition (proof lines 2191-2193): f : Nat -> Nat x Nat sends k to the tuple (n,m) occupying the n-th row and m-th column of the zig-zag array such that k is that tuple's position value in the enumeration.

Why f is an enumeration: the exhibit's traversal order (anti-diagonals of constant n+m, read bottom-left to top-right) visits every tuple exactly once, so every element of Nat x Nat appears at some finite stage k of the sequence.
proof_roadmap: Read f off the displayed zig-zag sequence.
Every tuple sits on some anti-diagonal, so the traversal reaches it.
